title: Living and Non-living Things
seo_title: Primary 3 Science: Living and Non-living Things Worksheets (with Answers)
standard_code: Primary 3: Diversity of living and non-living things (General characteristics)
standard_text: Identify the characteristics of living things: they need air, food and water, grow, respond to changes and reproduce. Classify things as living and non-living by observing their characteristics (summary of the MOE Primary Science Syllabus).
meta_desc: Free Primary 3 science worksheets for Singapore pupils on living and non-living things: needing air, food and water, growth, response and reproduction. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Living things need air, food and water.
key_sub: They also grow, respond to changes and reproduce.
body_html:
How to think about it

Living things share some characteristics.

  • They need air, food and water.
  • They grow.
  • They respond to changes around them.
  • They reproduce (make young or new plants).

Non-living things do not show all of these, even if they move or make sounds.

Example

A toy car moves when it is pushed. Is it living?

It does not need food or water

It does not grow or reproduce

Answer: No, it is non-living.

Example

A seed is put on wet cotton wool and grows a root. Is it living?

It grows

It can become a new plant

Answer: Yes, a seed is living.

Common mistakes

  • Thinking anything that moves is living. A fan, a cloud and a car move but are non-living.
  • Thinking plants are non-living because they do not walk. Plants grow, respond and reproduce.
  • Thinking seeds are dead. A seed is a living thing waiting to grow.
  • Forgetting that plants also need air.

faq.q: How do I know if something is living?
faq.a: Check whether it needs air, food and water, grows, responds to changes and reproduces. A living thing does all of these.

faq.q: Is a plant living if it does not move?
faq.a: Yes. Plants grow, respond to light and touch, and reproduce with seeds or spores, even though they do not move from place to place.

faq.q: Why is a fire not living?
faq.a: A fire can grow and needs air, but it does not reproduce or respond to changes like a living thing.

items.q: Which one of these is a non-living thing?
items.e: A rock does not grow or reproduce, even if it moves.

items.q: Is a mushroom a living thing?
c: No, because it has no leaves.
No, because it is not green.
No, because it does not move.
Yes. It needs food, water and air, grows and reproduces.
items.e: A mushroom is a fungus. Fungi are living things.

items.q: Is a fern a living thing?
c: Yes. It needs air, food and water, grows and reproduces.
No, because it does not move.
No. It does not grow or reproduce.
items.e: A fern is living, even though it does not move from place to place.

items.q: What do living things need to stay alive?
items.e: All living things need air, food and water.

items.q: Is a pandan plant a living thing?
c: Yes. It needs air, food and water, grows and reproduces.
No, because it does not move.
No. It does not grow or reproduce.
items.e: A pandan plant is living, even though it does not move from place to place.

items.q: Which one of these is a non-living thing?
items.e: A ceiling fan does not grow or reproduce, even if it moves.

items.q: Which one of these is a living thing?
items.e: A durian tree needs air, food and water, grows and reproduces.

items.q: How does a plant reproduce?
c: It moves to a new place.
It makes seeds or spores that grow into new plants.
It eats food from the soil.
items.e: Flowering plants make seeds; ferns and mosses make spores.

items.q: Is a guppy a living thing?
c: Yes. It needs air, food and water, grows and reproduces.
No, because it does not move.
No. It does not grow or reproduce.
items.e: A guppy is living.

items.q: Which living thing does NOT move from place to place?
items.e: Plants are living but do not move from place to place.

items.q: Which one of these is a living thing?
items.e: A mosquito needs air, food and water, grows and reproduces.

items.q: Is a hibiscus plant a living thing?
c: No, because it does not move.
Yes. It needs air, food and water, grows and reproduces.
No. It does not grow or reproduce.
items.e: A hibiscus plant is living, even though it does not move from place to place.

items.q: Is a seed a living thing?
c: No, only the plant is living.
No, it looks like a stone.
Yes. It can grow into a new plant when it gets water, air and warmth.
items.e: A seed is alive but resting until it germinates.

items.q: Is a television a living thing?
c: No, because it does not move.
No. It does not grow or reproduce.
Yes. It needs air, food and water, grows and reproduces.
items.e: A television is non-living.

items.q: Which of these shows that a mango tree grows?
c: It becomes taller and thicker over the years.
items.e: Growing means getting bigger over time.

items.q: Which of these shows that a cat responds to changes?
c: It runs away when a dog barks.
items.e: Responding means reacting to something around it.

items.q: Is an otter a living thing?
c: Yes. It needs air, food and water, grows and reproduces.
No. It does not grow or reproduce.
No, because it does not move.
items.e: An otter is living.

items.q: Which one of these is a non-living thing?
items.e: An MRT train does not grow or reproduce, even if it moves.

items.q: Which of these shows that a chicken reproduces?
c: It lays eggs that hatch into chicks.
items.e: Reproducing means making young.

items.q: Which one of these is a living thing?
items.e: A kitten needs air, food and water, grows and reproduces.

items.q: When you touch a mimosa (touch-me-not) plant, its leaves fold up. What does this show?
items.e: The leaves react to touch.

items.q: Which of these is a non-living thing?
items.e: A stone does not need food or reproduce.

items.q: A rock cannot feed. What does this tell us?
items.e: Living things need food. Plants make their own.

items.q: A sunflower turns towards the light. Which characteristic of living things does this show?
items.e: The plant reacts to the light.

items.q: Is a wooden chair a living thing?
c: No, because it does not move.
Yes. It needs air, food and water, grows and reproduces.
No. It does not grow or reproduce.
items.e: A wooden chair is non-living.

items.q: Which of these is true of ALL living things?
items.e: All living things need air, food and water, grow, respond to changes and reproduce. Not all of them has a heart.

items.q: A fish dies in a tank of water that has had the air removed. Which characteristic of living things does this show?
items.e: This shows the need for air.

items.q: Which of these is true of ALL living things?
items.e: All living things need air, food and water, grow, respond to changes and reproduce. Not all of them has a heart.

items.q: Which of these is a living thing that cannot move from place to place?
items.e: Plants are living even though they stay in one place.

items.q: Is a bicycle a living thing?
c: Yes. It needs air, food and water, grows and reproduces.
No, because it does not move.
No. It does not grow or reproduce.
items.e: A bicycle is non-living, even though it moves.

items.q: A toy dog walks and barks. Why is it NOT a living thing?
c: It does not need food, grow or reproduce.
It moves, so it is living.
It is made in a factory, so it is alive.
items.e: Moving and making sounds do not make something alive.

items.q: A rock cannot grow. What does this tell us?
items.e: Living things get bigger as they get older.

items.q: Why is a fire NOT a living thing, even though it grows bigger?
c: It does not reproduce or respond like a living thing.
items.e: A thing must show all the characteristics of living things.

items.q: A baby grows into an adult. Which characteristic of living things does this show?
items.e: Getting bigger and older is growth.

items.q: A caterpillar becomes larger after eating leaves. Which characteristic of living things does this show?
items.e: This shows growth.

items.q: The leaves of a mimosa plant fold when touched. Which characteristic of living things does this show?
items.e: This shows response to changes.

items.q: Is a rock a living thing?
c: Yes. It needs air, food and water, grows and reproduces.
No, because it does not move.
No. It does not grow or reproduce.
items.e: A rock is non-living.

items.q: Do plants need air?
c: Yes. All living things, including plants, need air.
Only plants that have flowers need air.
items.e: Plants need air, just like animals.

items.q: Which of these do ALL living things do?
items.e: Living things get bigger as they get older.

items.q: Which of these is true of ALL living things?
items.e: All living things need air, food and water, grow, respond to changes and reproduce. Not all of them is bigger than a person.

items.q: Is a ceiling fan a living thing?
c: Yes. It needs air, food and water, grows and reproduces.
No, because it does not move.
No. It does not grow or reproduce.
items.e: A ceiling fan is non-living, even though it moves.

items.q: Which of these do ALL living things do?
items.e: Living things make new living things like them.

items.q: Which of these do ALL living things do?
items.e: Living things can move by themselves. Plants move slowly, for example turning to the light.

items.q: Why is a wooden table non-living now?
c: It was once part of a tree but no longer grows or reproduces.
It was never part of a living thing.
items.e: The wood came from a living tree, but the table is not alive.

items.q: Which of these is NOT a characteristic of all living things?
items.e: Most living things cannot talk.

items.q: Which of these living things lays eggs?
items.e: Chickens reproduce by laying eggs; dogs, cows and cats give birth to young.

items.q: Is a seed a living thing?
c: No. It does not grow or reproduce.
Yes. It needs air, food and water, grows and reproduces.
No, because it does not move.
items.e: A seed is living, even though it does not move from place to place.

items.q: Is a metal spoon a living thing?
c: No, because it does not move.
No. It does not grow or reproduce.
Yes. It needs air, food and water, grows and reproduces.
items.e: A metal spoon is non-living.

items.q: Rachel says a toy robot is alive because it moves. What is wrong?
c: Robots are alive because they move.
A robot cannot feed, grow or have young, so it is not alive.
items.e: Living things can move by themselves. Plants move slowly, for example turning to the light.

items.q: A cloud is a non-living thing, although it moves and changes shape. Which of these can it NOT do?
items.e: Only living things can reproduce (make young or new plants).

items.q: Is a bread mould a living thing?
c: No. It does not grow or reproduce.
No, because it does not move.
Yes. It needs air, food and water, grows and reproduces.
items.e: A bread mould is living, even though it does not move from place to place.

items.q: A car is a non-living thing, although it moves and uses fuel. Which of these can it NOT do?
items.e: Only living things can reproduce (make young or new plants).

items.q: Which of these shows that a plant needs water?
c: A plant that is not watered wilts.
A plant grows in a pot.
items.e: Without water, a plant wilts and may die.

items.q: Fire grows and moves. Is it alive?
c: No. It does not feed, breathe and have young like living things.
items.e: Living things move, breathe, feed, grow and have young. Things that only move are not alive.

items.q: A cockroach runs away when the light is switched on. Which characteristic of living things does this show?
items.e: This shows response to changes.

items.q: A goldfish was put in a tank of boiled and cooled water with no air in it. What would happen?
c: It would be fine because it is in water.
It would turn into a plant.
It would die because it cannot get the air it needs.
items.e: Fish need the air dissolved in water.

items.q: Is a sparrow a living thing?
c: No, because it does not move.
Yes. It needs air, food and water, grows and reproduces.
No. It does not grow or reproduce.
items.e: A sparrow is living.

items.q: A fire is a non-living thing, although it gets bigger. Which of these can it NOT do?
items.e: Only living things can reproduce (make young or new plants).

items.q: Which of these living things gives birth to young alive?
items.e: Most mammals give birth to live young.

items.q: Siti kept a potted plant in a dark cupboard and gave it no water for 3 weeks. What most likely happened?
c: The plant grew taller and greener.
items.e: Living things need water to survive.

items.q: Is a candle flame a living thing?
c: No, because it does not move.
Yes. It needs air, food and water, grows and reproduces.
No. It does not grow or reproduce.
items.e: A candle flame is non-living, even though it moves.

items.q: A pupil blinks when a bright light shines in her eyes. Which characteristic of living things does this show?
items.e: This shows response to changes.

items.q: Is a rubber ball a living thing?
c: No. It does not grow or reproduce.
No, because it does not move.
Yes. It needs air, food and water, grows and reproduces.
items.e: A rubber ball is non-living, even though it moves.

items.q: Is a kite a living thing?
c: Yes. It needs air, food and water, grows and reproduces.
No. It does not grow or reproduce.
No, because it does not move.
items.e: A kite is non-living, even though it moves.

items.q: Do all living things grow?
c: No, living things stay the same.
Yes. They get bigger as they get older.
items.e: Growing is a sign of life.

items.q: Are plants alive?
c: Yes. They feed, grow and make seeds.
items.e: Plants are living things.

items.q: Which one of these is a non-living thing?
items.e: A robot vacuum cleaner does not grow or reproduce, even if it moves.

items.q: What does 'living' mean?
c: alive now: it feeds, grows, breathes and has young
it is made in a factory
items.e: Animals and plants are living.

items.q: Which one of these is a non-living thing?
items.e: A kite does not grow or reproduce, even if it moves.

items.q: Which one of these is a non-living thing?
items.e: A wooden chair does not grow or reproduce, even if it moves.

items.q: Which one of these is a living thing?
items.e: A mango tree needs air, food and water, grows and reproduces.

items.q: Which of these is living: a cotton T-shirt, a horse, a lump of clay or a steel can?
items.e: It is living: it can feed, grow and breathe.

items.q: Do all living things need food?
c: Yes. Animals eat; plants make their own food.
items.e: All living things feed.

items.q: Is a mosquito a living thing?
c: No. It does not grow or reproduce.
No, because it does not move.
Yes. It needs air, food and water, grows and reproduces.
items.e: A mosquito is living.

items.q: A balsam plant makes seeds that grow into new plants. Which characteristic of living things does this show?
items.e: This shows reproduction.

items.q: Which of these is living: a leather shoe, a pebble, a rabbit or a rock?
items.e: It is living: it can feed, grow and breathe.

items.q: A mosquito sucks blood to get food. Which characteristic of living things does this show?
items.e: This shows the need for food.

items.q: Is a river a living thing?
c: Yes. It needs air, food and water, grows and reproduces.
No, because it does not move.
No. It does not grow or reproduce.
items.e: A river is non-living, even though it moves.

items.q: A snail pulls into its shell when it is touched. Which characteristic of living things does this show?
items.e: This shows response to changes.

items.q: Which one of these is a living thing?
items.e: A mynah needs air, food and water, grows and reproduces.

items.q: Which of these do ALL living things do?
items.e: Living things need food. Plants make their own.

items.q: Is a stone a living thing?
c: No, because it does not move.
No. It does not grow or reproduce.
Yes. It needs air, food and water, grows and reproduces.
items.e: A stone is non-living.

items.q: A rock cannot breathe. What does this tell us?
items.e: Living things take in air.

items.q: A rain tree seedling becomes a big tree. Which characteristic of living things does this show?
items.e: This shows growth.

items.q: A log in a wood has mushrooms and beetles on it. Which are living?
items.e: The log was once alive.

items.q: A pupil watered one balsam plant every day and gave another no water. Everything else was the same. What is she finding out?
c: whether plants need water to survive
items.e: Only the water was different.

items.q: A plant on a windowsill bends towards the light. Which characteristic of living things does this show?
items.e: This shows response to changes.

items.q: Is a robot vacuum cleaner a living thing?
c: Yes. It needs air, food and water, grows and reproduces.
No, because it does not move.
No. It does not grow or reproduce.
items.e: A robot vacuum cleaner is non-living, even though it moves.

items.q: Mei Ling put some mealworms in a box with one dark end and one bright end. Most mealworms moved to the dark end. What does this show?
items.e: The mealworms reacted to the light by moving away.

items.q: Jun Jie says a cloud is living because it moves and gets bigger. What is the best reply?
c: A cloud does not need food, reproduce or respond like a living thing, so it is non-living.
A cloud is living only when it rains.
items.e: Moving and changing size are not enough.

items.q: A pupil sealed a small plant in an airtight jar and another in an open jar. Which plant is likely to stay healthy longer?
c: the plant in the open jar
the plant in the sealed jar
items.e: Plants need air to stay alive.

items.q: Is a mynah a living thing?
c: Yes. It needs air, food and water, grows and reproduces.
No, because it does not move.
No. It does not grow or reproduce.
items.e: A mynah is living.

items.q: A pupil put a cardboard box with a hole over a potted plant. After a week, the plant had bent towards the hole. Why?
c: The plant responds to light by growing towards it.
The plant moved to find water.
items.e: Plants respond to light.

items.q: Is a remote-control car a living thing?
c: Yes. It needs air, food and water, grows and reproduces.
No. It does not grow or reproduce.
No, because it does not move.
items.e: A remote-control car is non-living, even though it moves.

items.q: Why is a toy that walks and talks not alive?
c: It cannot feed, grow or have young.
items.e: Check all the signs.

items.q: Which observation would show that a snail is living?
c: It is found in the garden.
items.e: Growth is a characteristic of living things.

items.q: Two identical guppies were kept in tanks. One was fed; one was not fed for a long time. What does this experiment test?
c: whether guppies need food to stay alive
items.e: Only the food was different.

items.q: Ahmad left a slice of bread in a warm, damp place. After a week, mould grew on it. Which of these is living?
items.e: Mould is a fungus. It grows and reproduces.

items.q: Which of these do ALL living things do?
items.e: Living things take in air.

items.q: Ravi put green bean seeds on wet cotton wool. After 3 days, roots and shoots appeared. What does this show?
c: The seeds are living things that grow.
items.e: The seeds grew into seedlings, so they are living.
